correctness.rationale: The edge-root generators for a tree are linearly independent, so the unique Gaussian maximizer is indexed exactly by edge comparison signs; projected iid Gaussian coordinates preserve all differences. Conditional leaf agreements yield a(x,y)=xy+(1-x)(1-y) and the integral with central-edge indicator. The reflection symmetry, binomial expansion and integer beta integrations give the exact rational double sum. The star normalizer is an exact beta sum; its two binomial-endpoint terms dominate asymptotically. The weighted hub measures concentrate equally at (0,0) and (1,1), with independent exponential coordinate deficits after scaling; domination follows from a(x,y)<=exp(-(1-delta)(x+y)) for x,y<=delta<1/2. The central edge agrees with probability 1 for opposite corner types, and theta²+(1-theta)² for same types. The resulting factor 1-theta(1-theta), together with p²S_p,q²S_q->2, proves the all-sequence limit even at theta=0,1 when both leaf counts diverge. A standalone exact rational checker matches independent rank-permutation enumeration for seven parameter pairs. Its finite checks are not the proof of the limiting assertions.

originality.rationale: The full text of the 2021 graphical-zonotope deformation paper describes normal fans, deformations and their inequalities, not this exact bistar Gaussian cone-angle square sum or simultaneous-large-hub limit. The 2016 Gaussian zonotope-vertex paper supplies the sampling-to-normal-cone connection but not a double-star closed form. The 1985 same-up/down permutation result applies directly to path orientations, not the two-branching-hub asymptotic. A published tree-zonotope width-variance theorem concerns widths rather than maximizers. An earlier bistar symmetric-edge inball theorem concerns the convex hull of roots, not their Minkowski sum. Searches for random tree orientation agreements, squared linear-extension counts and double-star collision asymptotics revealed no prior statement implying the central result; an unindexed equivalence is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed all-tree linear-extension square-sum or solid-angle result may imply this exact double-star limit.

value.rationale: Squared Gaussian normal-cone weights give the probability of repeated vertices in randomized linear optimization, a motivated measure of geometric sampling concentration. Exact rational evaluation for arbitrary two-hub sizes and the nontrivial sharp balance law quantify a coupling penalty which distinguishes a large balanced bistar from two uncoupled large stars despite its exponentially many combinatorial vertices. This natural two-parameter infinite-family result is neither a routine path identity nor an arbitrary small-size census. The limits are exact and accompanied by an explicit independently checkable finite formula.
